articleTitle: Dual-orthogonal polarized Vivaldi antenna for ultra wideband applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a design of a dual polarized Vivaldi antenna. The problems that were met during the design of such an antenna are depicted and proper solutions are described. The prototype of the proposed antenna is introduced and finally the full characterization of the dual polarized antenna is given. Since UWB is originally a time domain based technique, a time domain characterization of the antenna is also included.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of lumped element Marchand baluns
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a novel design procedure for lumped element Marchand baluns is proposed. An analysis is performed on the balun structure in order to determine the conditions for ideal balun performance in terms of the lumped element values. The analysis is verified by two broadband designs centered around 22.75 GHz and differing only in terms of their impedance transformation ratio. EM simulation results on our proposed lumped element Marchand balun structure predicts an insertion loss of 4 dB and return loss of 40 dB at the design frequency of 22.75 GHz. The amplitude and phase imbalance is predicted to be better than 1 dB and 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>, respectively obtained over a wide 15 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design considerations of the RF front-end for high dynamic range digital radar receivers
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In optimizing high dynamic range digital radar receivers, some non-straight forward trade-offs in the design considerations of the RF front-end should be taken into account. The designer should pay more attention in particular to the noise figure degradation caused by the Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) and the linearity margin of every non-linear component in the receiver chain. An S-band IF sampling digital radar receiver design utilizing an 14-bit ADC is presented, theoretically analyzed and simulated by using Agilent Advanced Design System (ADS) software. Finally, simulation results are presented to demonstrate the validity of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Heuristic methods for automated microwave filter tuning
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes optimization methods applied in tuning of microwave filter assumed as ldquoblack-boxrdquo device. In this case any type of modeling is not required. Based on measured S-parameter data, without time consuming sensitivity analysis, only direct search and heuristics methods based on artificial intelligence can be used. Proper combination of such methods can be successfully applied in automated filter tuning.

articleTitle: Towards automated full-wave design of microwave circuits
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: To keep up with the fast development of wireless systems short design cycles are required. At the same time the pool of experienced engineers is limited. In order to remain competitive at the world marked companies will require new electronic design automation tools that are capable of automated design of high frequency circuits. Such tools do not exist yet but promising results have been obtained by using surrogate models constructed form data computed with full wave solvers. Being almost as accurate as electromagnetic simulations surrogate models allow one to explore the design space very quickly. These models can be used for the design in both frequency and, if used with a fast passivity enforcement scheme also in time domain. Combined with appropriate optimization techniques they allow a fast synthesis of complex circuits. The accuracy of the synthesis is so good that only a few full wave simulations are required to fine tune the design. As a results the design of complex circuits such as filters and multiplexers can be fully automated.

articleTitle: Characterization and modeling of random vector network analyzer measurement errors
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: We present a technique for characterizing and modeling random vector network analyzer measurement errors. These errors manifest themselves as random changes or drift of vector network analyzer calibration coefficients. We model a change of calibration coefficients as a set of small electrically lumped perturbations occurring at different locations in the vector network analyzer. We then use measurements of a highly reflective offset termination to determine electrical parameters and locations of these perturbations. Our technique is the first step toward developing a statistical description of random vector network analyzer measurement errors and accounting for them in the measurement uncertainty analysis.

articleTitle: Passive transmission line phase shifter at C-band in CMOS using lumped elements
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A passive transmission line phase shifter (TLPS) with lumped elements is implemented in a commercial 0.18 mum BiCMOS process. The phase shifter consumes no DC power, requires only one control voltage and has a size of only 1.3times0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> while offering a continuously adjustable phase shift of over 360deg. At 5.2 GHz and for 360deg phase control, the measured insertion loss amounts (7.3plusmn2) dB. To the knowledge of the authors, the circuit has the lowest insertion loss reported to date for a passive phase shifter integrated in silicon with 360deg phase control. The circuit is well suited for adaptive antenna combining in mobile receivers.

articleTitle: Treatment of the three strip coplanar lines on the ferrite
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper the investigations of a coplanar line consisting of three strips located on a longitudinally magnetized ferrite are presented. In the analysis of proposed structure the spectral domain approach (SDA) and the coupled mode method (CMM) are applied. The coupling coefficients for different dimensions of the ferrite line are determined. Moreover, the dispersion characteristics calculated using both methods (SDA and CMM) are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Characterization of microwave absorbing materials using a wideband T/R measurement technique
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Results of an investigation on various microwave absorbing materials developed at the Telecommunications Research Institute (PIT) are presented. The materials, composed of proprietary powders mixed with either classical liquid or modernized dry material bonder, were characterized with a wideband T/R method using 7-mm in-house made coaxial airline holders utilized also for the multiline TRL calibration of a vector network analyzer. Effects of different technology applied were verified by comparing the complex permittivity and permeability characteristics of the absorbers.

articleTitle: Textile body-worn exponentially tapered Vee antenna
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper describes a new design of a flexible wearable antenna. The design is based on the exponentially tapered Vee antenna geometry adapted for manufacturing using textile technologies (yarn based on copper fibers and polyester nonwovens). Experimentally obtained VSWR and radiation patterns demonstrate suitability of the antenna for the operation in body-worn wireless systems in the ISM band.

articleTitle: Comparison study of electromagnetic human interaction with various 2.4 GHz laptop integrated antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper compares the electromagnetic interactions between the user and laptop antennas for various ISM 2.4 GHz antenna types: sleeve dipole, Inverted-F, simple patch and novel microstrip wrapped elements. The freestanding and in-situ performance of each radiator is evaluated in terms of reflection coefficient, far field gain pattern and radiation efficiency. The human exposition to EM radiation is analyzed in terms of specific absorption rate (SAR).

articleTitle: Five-port transceiver for WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A direct conversion transceiver based on a five-port structure has been presented that is very suitable for WiMAX applications. The transceiver operates in a wide bandwidth of 2.3-3.8 GHz. This low cost transceiver covers two WiMAX bandwidths of 2.3-2.7 GHz and 3.3-3.8 GHz. The simulation results show the performance of transceiver for this application.

articleTitle: The empirical verification of the location method based on the doppler effect
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper deals with the new location method of radio wave sources, based on the Doppler effect. This unique approach was worked out on the ground of analytical solutions, that describe Doppler frequency in free-space propagation. In this method, position of the radio signal source is calculated on the basis of momentary frequency measurements taken by mobile receiver. Theoretical and simulating analysis of the presented methodology was made before empirical verification process was introduced. This analysis enabled to evaluate technical capabilities, precision and distance working range of this new location method. Following problems are discussed in this presentation: the review of present methods of radio signals sources location, general outline of the method on the basis of the Doppler effect and preliminary empirical verification results.

articleTitle: Fully integrated microwave reflectometers in multi-layer microstrip-slot technology for ultra wideband applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents the design of compact fully integrated six-port reflectometers, which, from scalar power measurements, are capable to determine the complex reflection coefficient over an ultra wide frequency band of 3.1 to 10.6GHz. These devices are formed by multi-layer microstrip/slot couplers and power dividers that are assembled without vias or wire cross-overs. An ultra wideband operation of these devices is confirmed by simulations in CST Microwave Studio and Agilent ADS.

articleTitle: Measurements of powders and liquids employing dielectric resonator technique
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Dielectric resonators have been used for measurements of the complex permittivity of medium and high loss dielectrics at frequency 2.45 GHz. The Dielectric Resonator technique is a very fast, convenient and accurate measurement technique to use especially when data at only one frequency or a small number of discrete frequencies is required.

articleTitle: Performance Comparisons of MIMO and Phased-Array Radar
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper focuses on the performance of MIMO beam and comparisons with the two-way beam (the receiving beam multiplied by transmitting one) of the phased-array radar. Two kinds of the colocated MIMO radar are introduced: full MIMO and partial MIMO. Theoretical analysis shows that the beam of full MIMO which employs all virtual array elements is identical to the two-way beam of the phased-array radar; the beam of partial MIMO which selects elements with different phase centers is narrower, but has a gain loss; partial MIMO can avoid aliasing in angle when the transmitting antennas is spaced at greater than half-wavelength spacing. Simulations verify theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Broadband microstrip reflectarray formed by double circular ring elements
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A single-layer microstrip reflectarray antenna composed of double-circular rings elements of variable sizes is presented. Compared to single microstrip patches or rings of rectangular or circular shape, the double circular ring elements offer much a larger phase variation range and lower phase slopes and lead to broader operation of a reflectarray. Using these elements, a prime-focus reflectarray operating at 10 GHz is designed and its performance is compared with counterparts employing conventional single resonant microstrip patch or ring elements. The computed results of gain variation with frequency demonstrate a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 51% for a linear reflectarray composed of 13 elements developed on a 6mm foam substrate.

articleTitle: Introduction to EMC pre-compliance testing
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A short introduction to EMI pre-compliance testing is described in the paper. Described are several methods for dealing with ambient disturbing signals. Further is described special equipment for pre-compliance testing.

articleTitle: A 40 Gbit/s transimpedance amplifier in 0.25 μm SiGe technology with ultra low power consumption
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this work, a transimpedance amplifier for optical communication links up to 40 Gbit/s is developed. The amplifier is designed to operate in an integrated receiver front-end together with a commercially available photo diode. The amplifier circuit consists of a four-stage architecture with an optimized input impedance and a high transimpedance over a large bandwidth. Manufactured in a 0.25 mum SiGe-BiCMOS technology, the amplifier achieves a measured power gain of 31 dB and a measured transimpedance of 73 dB Omega over a bandwidth of 30 GHz. The circuit consumes 32 mW and the chip area amounts to 0.187 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads.

articleTitle: Technique for model calibration in retro-modeling approach to electric permitivitty determination
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a 3-step procedure for calibration of the open-ended coaxial resonator designed for determination of complex electric permittivity of large samples is described. The presented calibration procedure has been designed as a part of retro-modelling technique based on comparing measurements with data obtained with an EM simulator. Using the described approach it is possible to adjust the numerical model of the resonator so that it matches the real structure, which is a prerequisite if properties of unknown media are to be determined.

articleTitle: A 250W 2.45GHZ-band solid-state pulsed source
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The solid-state microwave transmitters and sources have found wider and wider applications not only in radar systems, but also in many branch of industry and medicine. This paper presents development of a 250W compact solid-state pulse synthesized source operating around 2.45GHz, for medical equipment as an exciter of accelerator’s cavity. The source includes programmable PLL synthesizer, pulse former, 4-stage class C amplifier, DC supply and control block with microcontroller. The 250W peak power with a pulse width up to 15μs and 10% duty cycle is achieved by combining in a balanced configuration two 150W high power amplifiers. The output power level is controlled within 7dB dynamic range. The power droop during RF-pulse is less than 0.1dB for1% duty operation and 70ns pulse fall/rise time in the whole output power dynamic range The PLL synthesizer achieves more than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−7</sup> long-term stability (including pulling effect) and −80dBc/Hz@1kHz phase noises.

articleTitle: Wideband correlation processing in polarimetric radar with compound signals and simultaneous measurement of scattering matrix elements
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper wideband correlation processing is proposed for use in polarimetric radar with compound signals and simultaneous capabilities for measuring the scattering matrix elements. The processing technique does not affect the range and velocity characteristics of radar objects.

articleTitle: Optimization of a FDTD Code for Graphical Processing Units
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Modern graphics processing units (GPUs) provide high computational power which can significantly decrease simulation time. We present two implementations of the FDTD algorithm on GPU and compare their performance with the CPU version.

articleTitle: A second harmonic tuned power amplifier in LDMOS technology
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this contribution, the design and the experimental results of a power amplifier in LDMOS technology are reported. The amplifier has been designed to operate at 2.14 GHz and exploiting the output second harmonic to boost the obtainable performances. The measurement results shown an output power of 39 dBm and a drain efficiency greater than 50% at 2.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Localization in wireless sensor networks based on ZigBee platform
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper two different approaches to localization in wireless sensor networks are compared. One is an algorithm hardware implemented in CC2431 transceiver chip and the second one is a software algorithm implemented on embedded microcontroller core. The results of open air and indoor test are presented.

articleTitle: Phasing characteristics of variable size double rings of square or circular shape for design of a single layer microstrip reflectarray
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper reports on the investigations into phasing characteristics of a unit cell of a single-layer microstrip reflectarray including variable size double rings of square or circular shape. It is shown that if the rings are printed on a conventional dielectric substrate, the phasing characteristics of the unit cell exhibit the phase range well in excess of 360deg but with a sharp slope. By printing the double ring elements on a thick composite substrate formed by a thin laminate and thick foam a slower slope and a reduced range but still covering 360deg can be obtained. The use of such a unit cell can lead to a wideband design of a single layer microstrip reflectarray.

articleTitle: RF circuit block modeling via Kriging surrogates
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The use of replacement metamodels (global surrogate models) has become commonplace as a cost effective alternative for performing complex high fidelity computer simulations. Due to their compact formulation and negligible evaluation time, global surrogate models are very useful tools for exploring the design space, what-if analysis, optimization, and sensitivity analysis. In addition, multiple surrogate models can be chained together to easily model large scale systems where a direct, fullwave simulation would be too cumbersome. Two crucial aspects of global surrogate modeling are data collection (sequential design) and hyperparameter optimization. Kriging models have become very popular in many domains but have seen little application in electronics and electro-magnetism. In this paper we study the impact of different hyperparameter optimization algorithms and sampling strategies on the accuracy of Kriging models as applied to a low noise amplifier (LNA) RF circuit block.

articleTitle: Dispersion charactersitics and electric field distributions of modes propagating in the open electrically gyrotropic semiconductor rod waveguide
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Here we present the electrodynamical analysis of the circular cylindrical rod semiconductor n-InSb waveguide placed in the external longitudinal magnetic field. We have investigated electric field distributions of the main and fives higher modes propagating in the n-InSb waveguide at the frequency range from 60 GHz till 240 GHz. We have investigated only the higher hybrid modes HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</sub> and EH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mn</sub> with the same symmetry as the main mode when the azimuthal index m = 1. The waveguide radius is r = 1.5 mm and the electron concentration of the semiconductor n-InSb is N = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>,. We discovered that the electric field intensity of investigated hybrid modes is observed in the different cross-section places. This fact can be useful for an excitement of some required modes or creating controllable solid-state electronic devices.

articleTitle: Method of temperature stabilization of electrical parameters of S-band stripline circulators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents results of numerical and experimental investigations for finding conditions for temperature stabilisation of below resonance junction circulator parameters. To meet requirements the temperature characteristics of saturation magnetisation and static magnetic field have to be correlated.

articleTitle: Frequency domain measurements for an UWB imaging system
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Paper presents the evaluation of the frequency domain measurements applied to an ultra-wideband (UWB) imaging system. Principle of the system operation consist in revolving the object under test and recording reflected signals for subsequent angles of rotation. Approach discussed herein is based on the frequency domain measurements. After transformation to time domain, the approach becomes almost equivalent to a time domain one.

articleTitle: Dual — band waveguide circulator for C and X bands
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Design and measurement results of a dual — band waveguide circulator are presented. Results of electromagnetic simulations are also demonstrated and compared to their measurement equivalents. Several circulator designs, of different construction and utilizing different ferrite materials, are considered and one of them is chosen for further research.

articleTitle: Complex permittivity measurements of lossy liquids at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf> mode cylindrical cavity was used for accurate complex permittivity measurements of lossy liquids at frequencies 7.4 GHz and 7.8 GHz. The complex permittivity was evaluated from measured resonance frequencies and Q-factors of the cavity with and without liquid under test employing rigorous electromagnetic analysis of the resonant structure in the complex frequency domain. Influence of the complex permittivity on the conductor losses in the cavity was taken into account in the complex permittivity determination. Several reference liquids have been measured including methanol, ethanol, 2-propanol and water showing good agreement with literature data. Uncertainty budget discussion proved high accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: Tunable sphere and cubic dielectric resonator
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: New designs of tunable dielectric resonators (DR) are elaborated and studied. Sphere and cubic DR have an advantage before studied previously cylinder type DRs because tunable single sphere or cubic DR resonator has filter characteristic liked multi-resonator systems.

articleTitle: Synchronization systems for high energy particle accelerators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Currently developed high energy particle accelerators require synchronization of their high frequency electronic subsystems with very high accuracy reaching 10 fs for short term and 1 ps for long term periods. Taking into account the accelerator size of many kilometers with thousands of synchronized devices and signal frequencies reaching 3.9 GHz, the design of the synchronization system for the accelerator is a very challenging task. This paper contains a short description of the most important design issues of the synchronization system.

articleTitle: Wideband VNA Design with Bandwidth 1:53 by Multisixport Principle
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Paper presents multisixport principle and its benefits above classical sixport. The novel multisixport design is presented in practical example with its parameters as obtained bandwidth and standard deviation of measurement.

articleTitle: Multi-physical model of Gunn diode
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper deals with the multi-physical analysis of the Gun diode. The electrostatic, drift-diffusion and thermal phenomena are considered in the physical model of the component. The basic equations are summarized, and modeling issues are discussed. The analysis was performed in COMSOL Multiphysics using finite element method.

articleTitle: Discrete shape optimization method of a non-uniform transmission line — advantages and drawbacks
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a study on convergence of the direct discrete approach to the design of a non-uniform transmission line. The method was applied to a wide range of practical problems, including the design of microwave filters and impedance matching networks. The performance of the optimization algorithm was surprisingly good. The presented method is reliable and insensitive to numerical truncation errors. It doesnpsilat require a good starting point. Generated profiles satisfy technological constraints and are almost smooth.

articleTitle: The received phase dependence on antenna polarization
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Change of phase of the received voltage has been examined for elliptically polarized transmit antenna when rotating linearly polarized receive antenna. The Poincaré sphere explanation proposed by S. Pancharatnam [1] is presented analytically when applying the tangential polarization phasors representing both polarization and phase vectors of plane waves as well as their spinorial bases. A numerical example and results of measurements are attached.

articleTitle: Matched planar two-element antenna for ultra-wideband radiocommunication systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents theoretical analysis of two-element antenna for ultra-wideband application. Mathematical model of functional power parameters of general multiport array is introduced. Results of computer simulations of different matrices describing matched planar two-element microstrip antenna, power parameters and radiation patterns are described. Problem of broadband matching and radiation of UWB signal is mentioned.

articleTitle: Design of Small Reverberation Chamber for Handsets Testing
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents the design procedures and 3-D full-wave simulations of the electromagnetic field inside a small-sized reverberation chamber. The electric field inside the chamber is computed and the influence of small geometric details and asymmetries is investigated as well as the effect of different excitations and stirrers, and thus represents a reliable tool facilitating reverberation chamber optimization. The small reverberation chamber having dimensions 1.16x0.75x1.1 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is designed for investigations of handset antenna terminals.

articleTitle: Derivative superposition method for linearizing microwave amplifier
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A procedure for active element linearization via derivative superposition used for MESFET transistors is discussed in the paper. A method for description of transient characteristics of microwave field MESFET transistors, other than classic one, is presented. A solutions of a circuit for a microwave amplifier of high linearity and its characteristics obtained via simulation are also shown.

articleTitle: Time-dependent RF performance degradation modeling of AlGaN/GaN HFETs
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: High voltage HFET’s fabricated from the AlGaN/GaN heterojunction demonstrate excellent RF output power performance. The nitride HFET’s produce RF output power greater than an order of magnitude higher than available from GaAs and InP based devices. However, the HFETs demonstrate a reliability problem where the dc current and RF output power continually decrease as a function of time. The reliability problem is shown to be related to the conduction characteristics of the gate electrode and an electron tunneling mechanism where electrons leak from the gate to the surface of the semiconductor. In this work the physics responsible for this behavior are investigated and described. Physics-based models suitable for use in RF circuit harmonic-balance simulators have been developed, with excellent agreement between measured and simulated data.

articleTitle: Design and experimental investigations of UWB microstrip and stripline antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents two planar elliptical antennas for use in ultra-wideband radiocommunication systems: microstrip and stripline antennas. Design procedure of UWB antennas was described. Results of computer simulation and measurements are shown and discussed. Radiation of UWB signals by both antennas was analyzed. A new parameter - UWB antenna transmittance was introduced and used for analysis of signals emitted by antennas.

articleTitle: New planar dipole radiator for UWB application
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the paper the results of numerical study of a new dipole radiator for UWB applications are presented. The proposed dipole arm is combined with a triangle and trapezium. In order to find the optimal dimension of the dipole arm a suitable criterion was proposed. The results of the simulations confirmed that the proposed structure showed better matching than circular and elliptical structures. It was also found and verified numerically that the proposed dipole is characterised by an omni-directional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Mesurements of thin resistive films employing split post dielectric resonator technique
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Split post dielectric resonators have been used for measurements of the surface resistance of thin cermet and patterned metal films deposited on a thin low loss dielectric substrate.

articleTitle: Impact of non-ideal antennas on the performance of UWB imaging systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper the influence of non-ideal antennas on the quality of UWB imagery is analyzed. The frequency dependent patterns of different antennas are measured and inserted into a simulation model. The obtained raw data are focused using the Kirchhoff migration method and the positions of the simulated scatterers are extracted. Using these data the positioning error, resolution, and coverage of an imaging system are analyzed in connection to the antenna features.

articleTitle: Analysis of Luneburg lenses using domain decomposition method
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a method of electromagnetic analysis of Luneburg lenses is presented. The method combines three techniques, namely volume-integral equation/method-of-moments (VIE/MoM), the domain decomposition method (DDM) based on the surface equivalence principle, and the body-of-revolution (BoR) scheme. It is shown that application of DDM allows the user to pre-compute, or partially solve the computationally expansive sub-problem, involving volume formulation, and then put it into an external configuration of excitations, where only a relatively small linear set resulting from surface formulation has to be solved.

articleTitle: Flexible offline testbed for verification of new RF techniques and concepts
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper the conceptual design of a universal testing platform (testbed) based on SDR (software defined radio) paradigm for RF experiments targeting 700 MHzdivide2700 MHz frequency band is presented. The proposed solution is addressed to implementation and evaluation of new transmission techniques, RF architectures or modulation schemes. Testbed control, preparation of arbitrary modulation signals and no-real time post-processing of captured data are performed directly from Matlab. The expected performance of the overall system and characteristics of the major elements are discussed, including the analog frontend with direct up/down-conversion stage and PLL synthesized LO, DACs and ADCs, as well as baseband signal storage block (SRAM).

articleTitle: Evaluating power density in vicinity of commercial antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper analyzes results of numerical simulations of the electromagnetic field distribution in the near region of the dipole arrays used in base stations of mobile communication systems (the model of the antenna GSM900). The computation method is based on formulas for the near-field radiation of elementary dipole arrays. In order to verify results, computed near field and far field are compared to the results produced by Zeland IE3D.

articleTitle: Monopulse IFF antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Monopulse antennas purpose to work in short range interrogators which have monopulse pattern in two axes — in elevation and in azimuth is presented in the paper. The antennas example have been made in microstrip technology (based on dielectric substact). They have flat shape, which is a considerable advantage in many applications. This paper has shown principal problems concerning side lobes compensation in monopulse antennas. Has been discuss parameter’s antenna and also has shown analyses of radiation elements designs. Three different variants of summation-differential circuits have also been shown.

articleTitle: 23 GHz LNA with 1.5 V × 1 mA supply in low-fT SiGe technology
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A 23 GHz low noise amplifier using silicon germanium heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) is presented in this paper. It is demonstrated that low power consuming low noise amplifiers (LNAs) operating above 20 GHz can be designed with a low cost 60-GHz-f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub> BiCMOS technology. The fully integrated circuit has a die area of only 0.46 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. At 50 Omega terminations, a power gain of |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>| = 9.3 dB, a noise figure of NF = 4.3 dB, and an input-referred 1-dBcompression point of P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sub> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dB</sub> = -18.9 dBm are measured. The complete circuit consumes only 1.5 mW power with a supply voltage of 1.5 V and has to the authorpsilas knowledge the highest figure of merit reported to date.

articleTitle: Combined approach to analysis of resonators containing elliptical obstacles
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: An alternative method of analysis of elliptical post is presented. The method is based on a combination of elliptical and cylindrical coordinate systems. Proposed technique concerns single object only, however it can be easily extended to analysis of any set of the obstacles. To show the validity of the method three different kinds of resonators were examined. The results show a good agreement with analytical technique and FDFD (finite-difference frequency-domain) method.

articleTitle: A planar version of a slotline leaky wave antenna with a stacked substrate
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a new version of a leaky wave antenna based on a conductor-backed slotline with a stacked substrate. The advantage of this new structure is its flat top surface, due to the antenna being fed from the rear side via an SMA connector. The antenna radiates into a single main beam above the substrate. A bi-directional antenna radiating symmetrically both forwards and backwards was obtained by mirroring the structure.

articleTitle: Influence of multiple crossover and mutation to the convergence of genetic optimization
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper present original results of the numerical study of the multiple crossover and mutation to the convergence of the genetic optimization. The numerical study includes the minimization of special one- and two-dimensional functions, and also real functions from the area of computational electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Statistical VNA calibration technique using thru and multiple reflect terminations
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel statistical technique for calibrating vector network analyzer (VNA) with zero-length thru and multiple-reflect terminations is presented. The terminations are assumed to be of the same type, e.g. offset terminations of different lengths with partly unknown characteristics. Their reflection coefficients are modeled over frequency and identified in the calibration together with the VNA error terms. Experiments have verified high accuracy of this new technique.

articleTitle: Near field estimation of patch antennas from the fringing fields
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Determination of far fields using magnetic line currents has been found to be accurate. However, this approach fails when near fields are determined. The magnetic line currents determined from the Eigen functions were earlier determined along the periphery of a patch antenna. This approach was found to be sufficiently accurate only for the far fields. The accuracy of the near fields using this approach is found to deviate when compared to the full-wave model. This problem is overcome by modelling the fringing fields and incorporating this to analytical approach by which the Eigen functions are determined. Accurate modelling of near fields is a must especially for determining the magnetic interactive currents for patch antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Rigorous analysis of light scattering from multilayered gratings with biaxial anisotropy
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The rigorous coupled-wave approach (RCWA) is applied to analyze light scattering from one-dimensional lamellar multilayered gratings with biaxial anisotropy. Numerical results are presented for photoresist traces on a silicon substrate, showing the effect of anisotropy on the Stokes parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis of waveguide bends and resonator structures
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The analysis of microstrip and rectangular waveguide bends was described by the author by using the method of lines (MoL) with discretization lines of different length. In these algorithms the bend angle must be relatively small. In this paper, we show that we can combine the MoL with finite differences and how we can combine different coordinate systems in the different subparts of the structures. The algorithms then can be used also for other more complex devices.

articleTitle: MEMS-switchable microwave bandpass filter
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A K-band to Ku-band switchable microstrip bandpass filter is designed and fabricated. The filter response is switched using MEMS cantilever capacitive switches. The filter design and fabrication procedures are briefly discussed. The measured filter achieves 36.2 % of frequency switching range and exhibits insertion losses of 0.6 and 1.0 dB at 21.85 and 15.15 GHz respectively. To the best of our knowledge, the reported filter has the best insertion loss characteristic of all MEMS tunable microwave filters to date. The 6.7 GHz switched frequency band is also the widest absolute frequency range for MEMS tunable filters reported to date.

articleTitle: Thermal analysis of feasibility of air cooling system in S Band Transmit Module
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper describes thermal investigation of an S band transmit module with air cooling system. Temperatures of high power transistor junctions and temperature distribution in transmit module were computed by a professional computer tool. Due to intention of applying transmit module in an antenna cabin, the size of air-cooling system and air flow rate of the used fans were especially taken into account. The influence of cooling system parameters on temperature of transistors is presented. Results of measurements of the already developed and manufactured S band transmit module with liquid cooling system were compared with the results of its thermal simulation to prove the correctness of the thermal analysis.

articleTitle: Identification of radar signals using discriminant vectors
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: One of the most principal functions of the electronic intelligence (ELINT) system is gathering the basic information from the entire electromagnetic spectrum and its analysis. The paper presents some aspects of radar signals acquisition in ELINT system, the analysis of their parameters, feature extraction using discriminant vectors and linear Karhunen-Loeve transformation and their applying to identification of the intercepted signals.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering by periodic system of parallel-plate waveguides with thick walls
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Electromagnetic wave scattering by a periodic array of semi-infinite thick-walled parallel plate waveguides is studied in this paper. The scattered field in the free space above the waveguides is sought in the form of a series of spatial harmonics in accordance with the Floquetpsilas theorem, whereas in the waveguide regions it is sought in the form of parallel plate waveguide modes. To satisfy the boundary and edge conditions by field components in the free space above the array the use is made of certain Fourier expansion with corresponding coefficients being properly chosen Legendre functions. As a result, the amplitudes of spatial harmonics are given in the form of infinite series of Legendre functions with unknown coefficients being the solution of certain doubly infinite system of linear equations. The exact solution to the one can not be obtained, however, and numerical calculations are required to find the unknown expansion coefficients approximately.

articleTitle: A new scattering matrix of multiport antenna array
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper deals with the mathematical model and properties of a new scattering matrix of given antenna array normalized to complex multiport impedance matrix of generators. The introduced scattering matrix is described a matching problem for a connection of array with multiport beamformer. The scattering parameters are based on eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the antenna multiport matrices. As shown there are an infinite number of the scattering matrices for given antenna array and multiport beamformer. The extremum properties of the Rayleigh ratio for the power maximization for multiport networks are used. The particular array and excitation network (signal divider) and results of computer frequency characteristic simulations are described.

articleTitle: Homodyne single line phase noise measurement system for microwave oscillators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Proper measurement of phase noise for different oscillators is still a very problematic metrology issue. The most common way of measuring phase noise is the PLL technique, but it is complicated and efficient only when dealing with high stability crystal oscillators, masers, etc. In this article, we present the new concept of measuring phase noise, which is applicable especially for noisy oscillators working within the microwave bands. The whole concept of the measurement system is based on the single line discriminator method developed by Easdale, Dyer, Howes and Pollard. This system, enhanced with homodyne signal detection, significantly improves sensitivity and dynamic range of measurement, keeps the simplicity of the construction and calibration of the measurement system.

articleTitle: Green's Functions for Planar Structures: Frequency Domain Versus Time Domain
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A proper construction of Green’s functions for planar electromagnetic structures is the foremost task in the numerical analysis of microstrip antennas using integral equation techniques. In the paper, Green’s functions for a planar structure are formulated in the frequency domain and in the time domain. In the frequency domain, Sommerfeld type integrals are involved, and in the time domain, the Cagniard-de Hoop method is applied. In order to reduce high computational demands, approximate Green’s functions are frequently used. Near-field approximations of Green’s functions are presented and compared with rigorous Green’s functions to check their accuracy.

articleTitle: Modeling polysilicon capacitors and resistors for integrated circuits
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The aim of this paper to investigate the possible simplified equivalent circuits for resistors and capacitors made of poly layers in integrated circuits. Compromise has to be done when choosing device model regarding model accuracy and model complexity. This paper tries to find appropriate device models together with their limits.

articleTitle: A diagnostic system for active antenna transmit channels
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, an on-line diagnostic system design for active antenna transmit channels is presented. The system is based on cheap gain and phase solid-state meters, integrated with the transmit channels, for amplitude and phase pulse measurements during real transmit pulse. The measurement data analysis by comparison with the calibration data, at the level of a single detector is performed.

articleTitle: Phased array antenna with varactor phase shifters
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper concerns evaluation of the performance of the 4-element phased array antenna (PAA) equipped with varactor diode phase shifters. Steering of main lobe direction is available by selecting appropriate states of 4 phase shifters. Paper contains results of computer simulation and measurements. Scanning range verified by measurements appeared to fit the one obtained from computer simulation based on analytical solution.

articleTitle: Differintegral alpha-forms in electromagnetic theory of fractal antenna
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the present paper the concept of fractional calculus in terms of differintegral alpha-forms we apply to development of fractal antennas theory. The description of the nonuniform structured magnetic medium which are characterized by the entered magnetic moments, arises in problems of designing of antennas with electrical small sizes (fractal antennas) in immersing medium and in problems about radiation and interaction of electromagnetic waves on short distances in simulated medium. The model is based on the account scaling relations in measuring extent of the nonuniform set of points. An exact calculation of the radiation associated with the spherical modes of a alpha-linearly polarized antenna are given.

articleTitle: GaAs C-band 4-bit phase shifter MMIC
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes design and performance of a C-band monolithic phase shifter made in 0.18μm PHEMT technology for the phased array radar application. This compact 3mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> MMIC features extremely low phase error, fine VSWR and adequate insertion loss.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave CMOS miniature resonator and coupler
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: New millimeter-wave cavity resonator and broadside-coupled Lange coupler have been developed in a 0.25-μm CMOS process. The resonator employs a capacitively loaded cavity topology effectively implemented using the CMOS multi-metal-layer and via-hole structure. The CMOS cavity resonator, including two coupling apertures and microstrip feed-lines, occupies an area of 2 mm × 1.4 mm × 6.28 μm. It resonates at 30 GHz with a corresponding insertion loss of 2 dB and unloaded quality factor of 22.2. The broadside-coupled Lange coupler exhibits −3.3 to −3.35 dB through, − 3.3 to −3.7 dB coupling, more than 12 dB isolation and 15 dB return loss across 25–35 GHz while occupying only 217 x 185 μm of chip area.

articleTitle: Demonstrator of Class-S Power Amplifier for base stations based on GaN technology
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Demonstrator of a class-S power amplifier based on GaN transistors is presented. Input signal is generated externally in simulation tools (ADS, Matlab) based on a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order Bandpass Delta-Sigma modulator definition and a FPGA board is used as a signal source. The demonstrator is based on a Current Switching Class D (CSCD) topology. The presented solution offers an output power of at least 37 dBm (dependending on the supply voltage). Module efficiency is 20% (30% drain efficiency respectively) for full scale 3 GPP Delta-Sigma input signal. Center frequency is set to 225 MHz, with the posibility of increase for the purpose of analysis and measurements.

articleTitle: Kaiser-bessel window weighting function for polyphase pulse compression code
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper discusses and shows how the range-time sidelobes of P4 pulse compression waveform can be substantially reduced by applying Kaiser-Bessel amplitude weighting function. Also, a comparison is made with classical amplitude weighting function (i.e. Hamming window) applied to the receiver waveform of 100 element P4 code. Effects of weighting on the Doppler performance of the P4 code are presented.

articleTitle: Excitation of hypersound due to coupling with space charge waves of millimeter wave range in GaN films
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The excitation of hypersonic waves (f = 30 - 200 GHz) due to coupling with amplified space charge waves of the millimeter wave range in n-GaN films is investigated theoretically. Amplification of space charge waves due to the negative differential conductivity in GaN films placed onto a semi-infinite substrate is considered and possible spatial increments are calculated. The amplified space charge waves can excite hypersonic waves in the substrate at the same frequency due to piezoeffect and deformation potential mechanisms. It is demonstrated that the piezoeffect seems effective for resonant excitation of hypersonic waves.

articleTitle: Diffraction phenomena inside dielectric wedges — qualitative theory and verification by modelling and experiment
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A first order equation for determination of the strength of the edge overheating (diffraction) effect of foods and similar is developed and verified by modelling and experiment. In turns out that the power density is between 2 and 7 times higher in edges with between 60deg and 120deg edge angle than for a halfspace, for permittivities higher than about 16.

articleTitle: Fast multiplexer CAD using surrogate models for channel filters synthesis
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a fast approach to CAD of microwave manifold multiplexers using accurate surrogate models for channels synthesis. An example of three-channel multiplexer with dual-mode filters is presented showing remarkable performance of the approach.

articleTitle: Global stability analysis and stabilization of power amplifiers
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Power amplifiers often exhibit undesired behavior from certain input power value which cannot be predicted with a small-signal stability analysis. Among the commonly observed undesired phenomena are spurious oscillations, frequency divisions, hysteresis or chaos. In this contribution, simulation tools are presented, enabling an in-depth study of the origin and characteristics of these phenomena. The developed global stability analysis and stabilization tools have allowed an efficient suppression of the undesired behavior in a switching-mode power amplifier, with minimum degradation of the amplifier performance, in terms of drain efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: Class A power amplifier in 180 nm CMOS at C-band with integrated DC switch for efficient FMCW positioning radar
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A two stage class-A power amplifier optimized for FMCW positioning radar is presented. Fully integrated in 180 nm CMOS technology, the circuit features an integrated DC power supply switch for efficiency enhancements during the idle mode and RF isolation. The trade-offs for DC switch design and the corresponding speed implications are discussed. At a supply voltage of 2.4 V and a center frequency of 5.75 GHz, a RF gain of 12.5 dB, a 1 dB compression point of 17.3 dBm, and a RF isolation better than 28 dB at 3 dBm input power, are measured. Due to the DC switch a high drain efficiency of 16.2 % can be achieved over the full operation time of the positioning system.

articleTitle: Instrument for measuring the amplitude response of an RF-component for production testing
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper introduces a low-cost instrument which can measure the amplitude response of an RF component in the frequency range 700-2600 MHz with a dynamic range of 60-40 dB. The device consists of a PLL-based transmitter, a receiver based on a wide-band power detector IC and a PC-interface/control block. The device is specially designed for measurements in a production line for modern antennas, where the quality of antennas is assessed in terms of the pass-band peaks of a measurement jig combined with an antenna. The main benefit of the device is the saving in costs, when an expensive network analyzer can be replaced with this low- cost device. The device can measure the pass-band peaks with excellent repeatability, with a standard deviation of less than 188 kHz for frequency and less than 0.077 dB for amplitude.

articleTitle: On interaction of surface waves with thick elastic strips
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A system of periodic elastic strips (each one considered as a fragment of a plate) is characterized by a matrix relation between the Bloch series of displacements and stress at the bottom side of the system, contacting the substrate supporting the propagating Rayleigh wave. This characterization of strips, satisfying the energy conservation law with great accuracy, can be applied directly with the planar harmonic Green function characterizing the substrate in investigation of thick metal strips interaction with surface acoustic waves.

articleTitle: SACD algorithm of pulse stream analysis
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Final task of ESM (Electronic Support Measures) equipment is emitter identification. Identification in primary layer is based on processing of pulses stream existing on ESM equipment input. In this process each emitter is determined by set of parameters. Pulses in ESM equipment, during measurement process are associated with angle of arrival (AOA), frequency and time parameters. Those parameters constitute primary base for deinterleaving process. Time of arrival (TOA) is a basic parameter. It assures pulse repetition interval (PRI) estimation. PRI of radar signals usually is modulated in specific manner (e.g. stagger, sliding, dwell and switch) or in cyclic way and also it can have stochastic nature (e.g. jitter). Identification of PRI changes improves emitter description what has a considerable impact on recognition correctness. Detection of cycle in PRI modulation is relatively easy task from computation point of view and under assumption that acquired pulses stream can be associated with particular emitter. In practice due to antenna movement, ESM equipment acquires pulse trains (parts of pulses stream). Furthermore some pulses are missing and some additional pulses appear as result of noise and signal interaction. The methods of cycle detection presented in literature of problem have O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) computational complexity and require considerably big memory. The paper presents sequential algorithm of cycle detection (SACD) that has linear O(n) computational complexity. Results of examinations confirm high effectiveness of PRI parameters estimation for non-homogenous pulses stream.

articleTitle: Dispersion analysis of planar metallo-dielectric EBG structures in Ansoft HFSS
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the paper, the dispersion analysis of planar metallo-dielectric electromagnetic band gap (MD-EBG) structures in Ansoft HFSS is discussed. The attention is turned to critical settings of unit cell modeling for the correct computation of the dispersion diagram. First, a dispersion analysis of the original uniplanar compact photonic band gap (UC-PBG) structure was done, and the results were compared with the literature. Next, a dispersion analysis of a simple, a 3D planar EBG with the 1D periodicity, is presented. The existence of the surface wave band gap, predicted by the dispersion diagram, was verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Practical aspects of the doppler effect in mobile communication systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to conduct theoretical analysis and calculation of transmitter motion influence on received signal parameters. The form of the straight electric field and the Doppler frequency is the result of the theoretical analysis presented in this paper. To solve of the wave equation we have made use of integral transformations i.e. the Laplace transform (in relation to normalized time variable) and the Fourier transform (in relation to space variables). Finally, the practical time aspects of the location signal source measurement on the basis of the frequency Doppler is presented.

articleTitle: MIMO-OFDM system channel estimation based on subspace iteration
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Blind channel identification and equalization methods of oversampled MIMO-OFDM systems based on subspace are discussed. The proposed method employs reduced-rank orthogonal iteration to estimate noise subspace with low computational complexity. When the number of transmit antenna is greater than that of receive antenna of MIMO-OFDM system, oversampled method is used to obtain enough information for identification. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed method can achieve good performance.

articleTitle: Saw stabilised tunable microwave oscillator
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The new configuration of high frequency surface acoustic wave (SAW) oscillator has been presented in the paper. The circuit presented here is tunable and in this way flexible enough to collaborate with different kind of SAW devices like resonators or delay lines and does not require complicated calculation to design. It operates at higher harmonic frequencies and may utilizes the properties of low frequency SAW devices.

articleTitle: Noise-robust data fusion on a pixel level
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In present paper there was done analysis of possibility to use local correlation at pixel level data fusion in order to increase effectiveness of multilevel information fusion method.

articleTitle: A low cost 2nd harmonic trap for integrated radios
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel method is presented to reduce the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic level in low cost radios with balanced output configuration. The common mode- which is usually dominant at the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic frequency in differential configurations- is suppresed by a resonant trap which has no influence on the fundamental operation. The trap is applicable for differential antennas, baluns and matching networks and partly formed by them to minimize the cost. A novel matching balun circuit is also proposed for low cost ISM radio chips. With the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic trap the experiments showed ~12 dB 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic suppression improvement at 434 MHz using standard E21 0603 SMD elements. The new method was also demonstrated to be successful with printed loop antennas.

articleTitle: FDTD modeling of finite spot scatterometry
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this work, the FDTD method is applied to the modeling of finite spot scatterometry. Scatterometry is a non-imaging optical technique for extraction of parameters characterizing the quality of wafer processing in the IC industry. Several numerical methods have previously been adapted for scatterometry applications. However, infinite spot assumption has been inherent there. A Gaussian beam approach will be presented now as an alternative. It allows investigating the influence of reduced spot size on the accuracy of scatterometry techniques, with simultaneous economies in terms of wafer surface.

articleTitle: Newly developed chip sets for 60 GHz radio communication systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In order to reduce the manufacturing cost for future 60 GHz products, a high integration level is necessary. Recent results on mHEMT and pHEMT multifunctional receiver/transmitters realized at Chalmers University are reported. Multifunctional MMICs utilizing single ended, subharmonically pumped, balanced and single sideband mixers are reported. Recent system demonstrators include 60 GHz secure communication WLAN.

articleTitle: GPS receive antennas on satellites for precision orbit determination and meteorology
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The GPS satellites can be used for extremely precise orbit determination of satellites. This requires carrier phase detection, well known and stable phase characteristics of the antennas and on ground processing. Two antennas for this purpose have been developed by Saab Space, one small for the SWARM project, and a larger general purpose one. The GPS signals are also used for meteorology by the GRAS instrument on MetOp. The phase delays during occultations from a LEO satellite are measured using advanced array antennas.

articleTitle: An application of iterated function system attractor for specific radar source identification
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This article presents the procedure of radar source identification based on recognition of residually distinctive primal features using Linear Regression Method (LRM). It is kind of SEI method (Specific Emitter Identification), where Iterated Function System (IFS) is used to transform measurement points into transformation fractal represented as generalized measurement function. Further analysis of specific properties of this function leads us to extraction of distinctive features providing the method of exact identification of particular sources of radar emission.

articleTitle: Performance of 2×2 MIMO system utilizing various omnidirectional antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Present paper concerns performance of 2times2 MIMO system utilizing various omnidirectional antennas. Performed computer simulations have shown that symbol error rate of MIMO system utilizing simple monopole antenna is close to symbol error rate of MIMO system utilizing planar antenna with circular slot. This implies that in some applications monopole can be replaced by planar antenna, which is easier to manufacture, easier to integrate with microwave circuit, and resistant to mechanical damage.

articleTitle: Contact-less capacitive tuner for microwave comb-line mechanically-tuned filter
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents an approach to avoiding the problem of obtaining the electrical contact in typical tuners for stripline-based combline filters. The tuner structure shown here does not require any electrical contact and is based on the concept of the cylindrical capacitor with a sliding inner part. The idea of the construction and working principle are shown together with a simulation and measurement results for a manufactured model of 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order combline L-band filter.

articleTitle: Dual-band circuarly polarized spaceborne antenna made with multilayer composite lightweight panel
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents the low gain microstrip antenna developed for the Columbus laboratory of the International Space Station (ISS). The antenna manufactured with a state-of-the-art multilayer composite technology, operates in 1260-1270 MHz and 2400-2450 MHz. Its original main uses were planned in digital TV radioamateur services to be deployed by the volunteer organization Amateur Radio on International Space Station (ARISS) in a few years. Mechanical, thermal and material properties have been developed in a very careful manner to ensure antenna capability to sustain extreme launch loads and harsh space environment. The antenna had been developed with a participation of a few dozen institutions and our team as a primer with a particular strong support of European Space Agency, AOES, EADS Astrium and Thalesaleniaspace. Owing to their lightweight and thin profile, antennas could have been mounted on Columbus Meteorite Debris Panels on Earth at the Spacecraft Processing Facility. It made possible to reduce tasks during extra vehicular activities (EVA) and simplified module installation at the ISS.

articleTitle: The estimation of simultaneous signals frequencies in the IFM receiver using parametric methods
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the paper the approach using two special parametric methods to measure the frequencies of two simultaneous signals in the IFM receiver has been presented. Both algorithms have based on the assumption that the IFM receiver generates the autocorrelation, which can be used to determine two simultaneous signals frequencies. Some differences and similarities between both methods as well as problems that stem from this approach have been indicated. Experimental data have been shown and compared to simulation results.

articleTitle: Tapered slot antenna with reduced backward radiation
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Preliminary results of tapered slot traveling wave antenna design with reduced backward radiation are presented in the paper. The design combines properties of Vivaldi antenna and double ridge horn to obtain ultra-wideband directional antenna operating in 0.5–3 GHz band having small dimensions.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of composite aircraft model for HIRF testing
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A method of modeling a small aircraft with composite parts is described. The model is tailored to simulate the influence of a HIRF environment. In order to simplify the analysis, the dielectric material with suitable parameters is used instead of a complicated composite structure. The influence of composite parts on electromagnetic properties of the model is illustrated by electric field distributions at frequencies 1 GHz and 700 MHz.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic properties of the waveguide with layered periodic walls
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper is devoted to the theoretical investigation of the properties of the waveguide with periodic layered walls. We consider the waveguide formed by the gap between two periodic both dielectric and semiconductor structures. Various kinds of the field distribution are analyzed. Te influence of the external magnetic field on the waveguide properties is investigated. The nonlinear properties of the dielectric guiding layer confined between two periodic structures are considered. The condition under which the second harmonic intensity considerable increases is obtained.

articleTitle: Identification of frequencies and amplitudes of microwave simultaneous signals by means of IFM methods
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The basic specification and principle of operation of instantaneous frequency measurement IFM receiver based on microwave frequency discriminator MFD utilizes interferometric techniques is presented. Simultaneous signals measurement error was calculated. The method of measurement of parameters of signals coincident in time was proposed. This method uses only two parallel MFDs aided by digital processor. The processor evaluates two pair of IQ components, which the next build the digital image in form of the constellation diagram. The analysis of this constellation gives correct information about frequencies of each of simultaneous signals and about their amplitudes as well. The image processing or database techniques can be used for this analysis.

articleTitle: Efficient wideband analysis of electromagnetic problems using the awe adaptive technique with the hybrid MoM-FDTD method
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The use of a hybrid MoM-FDTD method can be effective for solutions of electromagnetic scattering and radiation problems, which are intractable for single full-wave numerical methods. In this paper we demonstrate a possibility of increasing computational efficiency of the hybrid MoM-FDTD method for obtaining broadband antenna response by employing the asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) technique in the MoM domain.

articleTitle: Terahertz waves and perspectives of terahertz biomedical technologies development
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The diagram of comparative development of frequency bands and powers by modern radioelectronic means and apparatus for biomedical technologies has been made up. Terminology and physical basis of selection of the terahertz band of electromagnetic waves are given. Comparative energy characteristics of terahertz and extremely-high frequencies waves are presented, tables of molecular spectrums of atmospheric gases, metabolites, air pollutants, some macro- and microbiological structures, frequency bands of relic background and some substances in the terahertz band are given. It is paid attention to some effects of terahertz waves interaction with biological and physical mediums. The perspective trends of investigations for creation of novel terahertz biomedical technologies are founded. The results of Daphnia magna Strauspsila functional state investigation depending on influence of atmospheric air, exposed to terahertz electromagnetic irradiation, on Daphnia water environment are presented. Also, the investigation results of Daphnia heartbeats frequency change during simultaneous effect of phenol, alternating magnetic field and electromagnetic radiation are given.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency polarimetric radar earth observations
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The air-borne multi-frequency polarimetric SAR ldquoIMARCrdquo allows radar earth observation measurements at 4 frequency bands (X,L,P and VHF) and utilizes a complete set of different linear polarizations: VV, HH, VH and HV.
