Theoretical and experimental feasibilities have been carried out in recent years. System capabilities and potential applications have been demonstrated. Operational usage in a wide range of applications is expected. However, from our research it became obvious that despite interesting data can be collected the major limitation of full and reliable utilization in various applications comes from the mismatch between available electro-magnetic models and the description of the actual earth surface and sub-surface during the SAR measurement campaigns. Applications are foreseen in hydrology and in classifying vegetation, snow, ice and frozen soils, and in sub-surface sensing for locating artificial and natural objects, as well as different natural anomalies. New and more advanced electro-magnetic modeling is needed in order to exploit all IMARC potentials. In the framework of a large multi-national activity an integrated software package will be developed in which new and more-advanced vegetation surface and sub-surface scattering models are included.

articleTitle: SOI beyond CMOS
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: SOI (silicon-on-insulator) technology has been proposed to improve performance of integrated circuits (ICs) fabricated usually in CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor) bulk technology. A SOI wafer consists of a thin monocrystalline Si film over an insulating layer of silicon dioxide (buried oxide - BOX) on a Si substrate playing for traditional IC application a role of a mechanical support. An electronic circuitry is usually fabricated in the top silicon film. Recently non-CMOS applications of SOI substrates play more and more important role. In late 90s, SOI technology has become a viable approach for both high performance microelectronics as well as for sophisticated micro- and nanosystems.

articleTitle: Load curve estimation for microwave ovens: Experiments and electromagnetic modelling
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Load curves of two representative household microwave ovens are constructed experimentally and by electromagnetic simulations. The load curve shows power dissipated in a water load as a function of the load size, and is considered a measure of oven performance. The paper points to several assumptions inherent in the standard experimental procedure and provides their field-theoretical sense. Further, measured and simulated load curves are shown in good agreement for loads above 0.2 l. For small loads, the measured values fall within a wider band between the numerically predicted maximum and minimum dissipated power values, which result from uncertainty of the magnetron operating frequencies combined with the resonant character of the reflection coefficient curves.

articleTitle: Directional antenna for EAS systems.
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Design and realization of a directional antenna for EAS systems is presented. Nowadays the coil antennas are used in anti-shoplifting systems. Coil antennas radiate uniformly in all directions perpendicular to the coil axis leading to waste of energy and electromagnetic pollution. The new type of the antenna having directional property and a simple structure is more efficient and environmentally safer. The trial antenna has been designed and measured. The design was based on electromagnetic simulations carried out in 3D electromagnetic simulator QuickWave. The near field of the antenna was optimized. The structure of the antenna enables a simple and cost effective fabrication process.

articleTitle: H- modes of rectangular dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The integral and integrodifferential equations and functionals in two-dimensional dielectric waveguide cross-section region and the iteration algorithms of their solutions have been considered. The parameters of H-modes are determined numerically for square dielectric waveguide.

articleTitle: Properties of microwave dielectrics with relative permittivity ε′ = 40 ÷ 90 and dielectric loss tgδε ≪ 10−3 manufactured on the base of titanates (doped with ions of metals from the lanthanum group)
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper elaborates on some aspects of the technology developing of a new group of microwave dielectrics with ε′ = 40 ÷ 90 based on titanates and their mixtures, especially on the base of barium titanates doped with ions of metals from the lanthanum group Re =≫ Sm, Gd, Nd, La, Pr. All dielectrics were manufactured by the typical ceramics technology. The dielectric parameters such as ε′ and tgδ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf> have been measured by the Rayleigh-Ritz resonant method as well as in constant room temparature as in the function of variable temperature.

articleTitle: The analysis of frequency modulated signals based on the IFM receiver
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The multichannel IFM receiver performance for intrapulse analysis of the frequency modulated signals in the microwave frequency band have been presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Reliability of the design method for optimized multiloop Opto-Electronic Oscillators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Applying the optimization method proposed by the authors previously for creating high-Q multiloop opto-electronic oscillators (OEO) with single mode operation may draw questions about the systempsilas sensitivity to the accuracy of the optimal parameter settings. This paper concentrates on the theoretical investigations of the question above to show that accurately calculated optimized parameters to be set are not against the proper realization of such a system.

articleTitle: Implementing Smart Antenna System using Genetic Algorithm and Artificial Immune System
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The current antenna systems have limited capacity when it comes to the frequency usage. Smart antennas provide a smart solution to this problem by steering the beam power in the desired direction and pointing nulls in the undesired direction. Genetic Algorithm is an optimization algorithm which mimics the underlying phenomenon of evolution of natural species and genetic recombination. In this paper we propose an application of genetic algorithm towards the implementation of two important properties of smart antenna system which are the direction of arrival detection and beamforming. Here we also incorporate the property of dasiamemorypsila from artificial immune system to make the system faster.

articleTitle: The influence examination of dielectric parameters on bandwidth in multilayer aperture-coupled microstrip antennas with utilization the FDTD method.
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The object of this article is usage of the FTDT method to analysis of planar antennas. The matter of Yeepsilas cell as a basic element of characteristic of filed in FTDT method and well as Yeepsilas algorithm are presented. The question of source modeling and stimulation of antenna, boundary conditions and method of analysis of planar antennas structure are also discussed. Some results of usage of the method have also been presented, as a confirmation of accuracy and usefulness for analysis of planar antennas. Aperture coupled microstrip antenna represents very broad bandwidth, lightweight, rigid construction. This type antenna has much better parameters like different type of microstrip antennas.

articleTitle: Different implementations of parallel processing for FDTD simulator
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Parallel processing in FDTD as well as other electromagnetic simulation methods is growing in importance. It allows not only to calculate faster but also to cope with large structures. Parallel processing can be implemented in different ways. The implementation depends mainly on computer architecture and programming libraries under different operating systems. Usually, different approach has to be taken also for a newly created program in contrary to rebuilding existing serial program into a parallel version. A European project for development of a parallel version of existing, professional FDTD simulator is presented. The simulator was principally designated for serial execution. Consecutive steps of code transition from serial into versatile parallel version are described.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic excitation of a finite cone by the ring slot: Axial symmetric case
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The scattering of the axial-symmetric TM-wave by the finite cone is investigated using the analytical regularization method. The characteristics of the far field pattern and the distribution of the electromagnetic energy emitted by the slot located on the conical screen are analysed. The physical effects connected with electromagnetic wave radiation by the electro dynamic system "cone-slot" are studied.

articleTitle: Low-cost handheld multiprobe reflectometer for the ISM band
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper we present a design procedure and a working model of low-cost handheld complex reflection coefficient tester for the ISM band. The tester is based on the concept of mutliprobe reflectometer and uses the integrated Analog Devices AD8318 power detectors. Measurements are controlled by the Atmel ATMega32 microcontroller. A prototype tester with friendly user interface was designed and realized for 2.3 – 2.6 GHz range, covering the lower WiFi band. Results of numerical simulations and experimental tests are presented.

articleTitle: Chaotic behavior of noise suppressed solid state lasers used in radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Optoelectronic reduction of intensity noise is presented for solid-state lasers. However the noise suppression feedback loop can make the laser operate in its chaotic regime. The paper shows the way to chaos through bifurcations at different levels of the feedback signal. Additionally a limit for chaos free operation is also given. The bifurcation diagram of the controlled laser is calculated as well.

articleTitle: GaN technology for microwave applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: GaN-based devices are currently developed in close collaboration with end-users. 10 years have been necessary to arrive at the edge of this development cycle. This paper will present the status of current AlGaN/GaN technology.

articleTitle: Small-sized helicon isolators for meter wave range
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Factors influence the dimensions of helicon isolators are researched. The limiting relation between cross sizes and thickness of helicon resonator are resulted. Characteristics of small-sized helicon isolator for meter wave range are presented.

articleTitle: New design method for noise suppressing optical-microwave filters
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper reports on a new design method developed for realization of optical-microwave filter structures for laser noise suppression applications. In addition phase-to-intensity noise conversion characteristics is calculated in order to exactly determine its limiting effect regarding noise reduction. Based on these calculations a new design way is presented for minimizing noise conversion and thus ensuring the proper operation of the noise suppression.

articleTitle: Analysis of electrically large problems using the hybrid MM-PO method
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Supporting the moment method (MM) formulation by the physical optics (PO) approximation is the well-known prospective way towards improving computational efficiency of MM-based approach at higher frequencies. In this paper, the results of numerical analysis of electrically-large, cannonical problems using the MM-PO hybrid method are presented. The goal of the analysis is to examine the offered saving in terms of both CPU time and memory storage relative to the conventional MM approach.

articleTitle: Optimum design of satellite TV antennas for weak signal environment
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes a process of optimization of corrugated horn feeds for satellite TV antenna applications. Optimization of the feeds was performed using an axisymmetrical version of a Finite Difference Time Domain software. The optimized horns were manufactured in high volume using CNC machines and applied in many TV installations in Cyprus. It is shown that typically more than 1 dB can be gained in the signal-to-noise ratio by optimizing the feed. Practical experience from application of the optimized horns shows that, to achieve the same effect of improvement of antenna performance, investment in horn optimization may be more than an order of magnitude smaller than investment in the increase of reflector size.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband radar target modeling using triangular patch model
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: To understand the UWB radar system, target scattering performance must be studied. As a widely used model in time domain electromagnetics triangular patch model (TPM) is employed to simulate UWB radar targets. But when the scattered fields are treated, singular points would occur of TPM. The singularity analysis is carried out of TPM and a method is proposed to deal with all kinds of singular points. The method proves effective through an application example.

articleTitle: Fractional-ratio frequency multiplier
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Technique for achieving frequency multiplication by fractional ratio is introduced. Typical offset phase-locked loop utilizes mixer to downconvert feedback signal to much lower frequency. It is well known that mixer generates another product at frequency equal to sum of mixer input frequencies. However, the sum product is usually discarded. Configuration of the offset phase-locked loop utilizing the sum product is proposed here. Frequency synthesis of 16.9 GHz from 8.5 GHz signal, using off-the-shelf components, is demonstrated.

articleTitle: UWB RoF system for in-vehicle applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A Radio over Fibre (RoF) system design and performance study of a full-duplex transmission Ultra Wide Band (UWB) radio directly modulated over a MultiMode Fibre (MMF) network for in-vehicle applications is reported. A comprehensive evaluation of the UWB radio transmission characteristics through the relatively inexpensive system and performance comparison of the Bit Error Rate (BER) is presented.

articleTitle: EBG Substrates: Myths and Reality
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A comparative study of two approaches to the design of planar antennas on EBG substrates is presented in the paper. Attention is focused to the match between the required parameters of the designed antennas and obtained ones. The final discussion results in methodological recommendations, which can ensure a proper functionality of the designed structure.

articleTitle: Planar antennas on EBG substrate - the gap selection
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper focuses on the applicability of electromagnetic band gap structures in the domain of antennas to suppress surface waves if used as a substrate. For the simplicity monopole antenna together with grounding plane was studied and results of far field is simulated and compared. Far field pattern and the influence of gap selection is further studied. Convenience of both guiding and radiating bands for application in the domain of antenna structures to suppress side lobes is discussed.

articleTitle: Electrostatics of quasiperiodic system of conducting strips
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The analyzed planar system of strips originates from an infinite periodic system by inclusion of the narrower strip and spacing in the middle of the system. This breaks the system periodicity making it quasi-periodic, as the system remains periodic outside of the inclusion. A method for analyzing such the structures is presented. Analogous systems are applied in the Fabry-Perot resonators, for instance. Numerical examples present the electric field in the plane of strips in both spectral and spatial domains.

articleTitle: Scattering matrix description of analog fibre optical links
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, we describe model of an analog fibre optical link. In the result of above we received of the scattering matrix of an analog fibre optical link. We have present the basic parameters of an analog fibre optical link.

articleTitle: Nearly perfect right angle bends
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The new geometry of right angle bends is developed. The concept can be applied to any type of a transmission line. Examples of bends in rectangular waveguides, strip lines and microstrip lines are presented. Waveguide bends have return loss better than 35 dB in full TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode operation range. Strip line bends have return loss better than 40 dB up to 25 GHz and microstrip line bends have return loss better than 25 dB up to 20 GHz. The optimization of bends has been performed in FDTD electromagnetic simulator.

articleTitle: Tunneling properties of multilayered periodic structures
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of electromagnetic wave scattering by multilayered periodic structure composed of cylindrical posts which constitutes a two-dimensional (2-D) electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure. The presented procedure combines several efficient numerical techniques, such as the iterative scattering procedure (ISP), the orthogonal expansion method, the T-matrix approach and the lattice sums technique. A simple and accurate cascading procedure is utilized to calculate the scattering parameters of the entire EBG structure. The effect of complete wave tunneling through the proposed structure and the procedure of controlling the tunnelled wave are discussed here.

articleTitle: Experimental satellite laboratory but education and research
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Since early nineties we are involved into program of international organization AMSAT. We have participated on several satellite projects as well as these satellites control and telemetry gathering. For this purposes we built up an automatic tracking system with high gain antennas and radio electronics for advanced spacecraft application. A number of graduate and postgraduate student projects became hardware and software application for this station. It has also been a good opportunity for students to meet spacecraft technology. Several of our activities in this field are described in this paper.

articleTitle: The influence of edge effects on the axial-symmetrical antennas beamforming
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The effect of finite ground plane on the beam-forming of axial-symmetrical antennas as the different designs of cylindrical monopole antenna with coaxial feeding line is studied. The features of near-field distribution in the inductive region of this class of antennas are analyzed. Depending on the geometric and physical parameters of antenna the conditions of radiation pattern transformation from mono-beam to multibeam one are determined.

articleTitle: Effective 8mm-Band (30–38 GHz) compact feed for multi-beam radio telescope: Simulation and measurement results
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A compact smooth-walled spline-profile horn covering the 30-38 GHz frequency band (8 mm radioastronomy band) to be used in a multibeam receiving array of a radio telescope has been optimized, manufactured and tested. The radiation pattern of this horn has sidelobe levels less than -24 dB in both principal planes across the band, cross-polarization levels better than -20 dB, input return losses better than 20 dB and the 3 dB-beamwidth is of the order of 40deg over the frequency band. Mutual-coupling of adjacent horns is less than -38 dB. We consider such a horn as one of the best candidates for an array feed for a multi-beam radio telescope.

articleTitle: A new method for measuring am compression and AM-to-PM conversion of microwave amplifiers
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The measurement of the nonlinearity characteristics is usually cumbersome. In this paper a simple method is presented for the measurement of some nonlinearity characteristics, i.e. for the AM compression and AM-to-PM conversion. These methods offer easy measurement processes that are widely applicable and do not need special instrumentation. They have another important advantage: the dynamic behavior of the AM compression and AM-to-PM conversion characteristics can also be obtained in a simple way. Using these measurement methods the AM compression and AM-to-PM conversion characteristics of a microwave amplifier have been tested.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the eigen modes for the modern gyrotron resonators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Rigorous mathematical methods are proposed to study eigen TE and TM modes of the corrugated resonators for the modern ITER relevant coaxial gyrotrons. These techniques could be used for the numerical analysis of the gyrotron resonators with the arbitrary corrugation parameters, moreover arbitrary mode numbers can be considered. Simulations performed based on these theories, results of the novel numerical investigations are presented and validated. Obtained results can be used to project and develop efficient modern gyrotron resonators.

articleTitle: SIC MESFET class E microwave power amplifier
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The simulation and experimental analysis of SiC MESFET class E power amplifier with enhanced frequency band was carried out. A specific multi-resonant output matching network was used to obtain required load impedance at the drain of transistor within desired bandwidth. The effect of transistor on-resistance on efficiency of power amplifier was considered. In the bandwidth of 800-1070 MHz output power of 2.5 W with power-added efficiency of 48% and DC supply voltage of 15 V was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Tunable bandpass filter based on surface wave resonator for 6-mm waveband
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The high-temperature superconducting (HTS) films on dielectric substrates were used successfully for creation of microwave X- and Ka-band planar filter with extremely low losses within the bandpass. These narrow bandpass filter are based on the surface wave resonator (SWR), which is coupled to a ferrite thin film. The filters are tunable by a DC magnetic field. We determined the coupled oscillations of gyrotropic YIG film with isotropic SWR in the frame of the magnetostatic approach. Using this theory and experimental results for X- and Ka-band filters we presume the microwave performance of coupled system of HTS and YIG films in 6-mm waveband.

articleTitle: 1.5 kW S Band Transmit Module
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: the paper describes S-band Transmit Modules designed for use in an Active Phased Array and Solid State Radar Transmitter. Brief principles of its operation are described and electrical and mechanical information are presented. Main parameters of Transmit Module are shown in the form of characteristics. Results of measurements in wide range of the ambient temperature are presented as well. Basing on the obtained results, conditions of Transmit Module operation are defined.

articleTitle: Direction finding device with eight element circular antenna array
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The wide-band direction finding (DF) device scanning entire space in azimuth has been presented in the paper. It contains a circular antenna array and the Butler matrix as a microwave amplitude-phase converter. The experimental version of the device works with microwave phase discriminator (MPD) and personal computer (PC). The method and results of theoretical analysis as well as measurements in the range of 2 - 4 GHz are also presented.

articleTitle: Investigations into microwave properties of various substances to develop a breast phantom for a UWB breast tumour radar detecting system
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper reports on experimental investigations into microwave properties of various materials that can be used to imitate real tissues in a breast phantom for testing an ultra wide band breast cancer radar detection system. The experiments involve an open ended probe technique to measure permittivity of selected materials across an ultra wide frequency band from 2 to 15GHz.

articleTitle: Point scatterers target identification using frequency domain signal processing
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The coherent ultra short pulse radar provides high resolution image of the target. A model of this image is composed in the superposition form by complex envelope of signals returned from point scatterers. In accordance with their positions and reflection coefficients the values of complex envelope are distributed over radar image coordinate plane. Radar image model is based on the known radar pulse envelope and a pattern of the antenna. The parameters of the target point scatterers are processed in the frequency domain using one dimensional data extracted from the complex discrete Fourier transform of the radar image. The Matrix pencil algorithm is used for the parametrical target identification. This approach is characterized by the ambiguity of the point scatterers positioning in the coordinate plane. Rotation of the image axes is used to provide a disambiguation.

articleTitle: S-band MMIC 6-bit phase shifter
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes the first pass design and measurements results of a single chip, 6-bit phase shifter. This phase shifter exhibits good VSWR, quite low insertion loss with low variation and correct phase performance over all 64 states across the entire 3-3.6 GHz band. Moreover, the design assures high level of P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> and good stability with regard to temperature variation.

articleTitle: Analysis of an internal mutual couplings influence on a radiation pattern of a nonresonant multislots waveguide array antenna
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a design method of a nonresonant multislots waveguide array antenna is described. The internal mutual couplings between adjacent radiating slots are considered in the presented wave method. Additionally a correction stage including nonresonant slot lengths is introduced in design method in order to evaluate an internal mutual couplings influence on antenna radiation pattern. As an example a waveguide antenna with radiating slots cut across a narrow wall of an air rectangular waveguide is analyzed.

articleTitle: Microwave breast tumor detection exploiting wideband Jacobians
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Gradient-based iterative algorithms are preferred in microwave tomography due to their fast convergence despite the fact that the solution is only local. The drawback is that response Jacobians are not available with current commercial electromagnetic solvers and reconstruction algorithms have to be equipped with in-house codes specifically designed to produce response derivatives in addition to the responses themselves. Even with in-house codes, the computation of the response Jacobians in a wide frequency band is a challenge. Here, we present an efficient approach to the computation of wideband response Jacobians with time-domain solvers. Through this approach, the Jacobian distributions (maps) of imaged regions can be computed with relatively small memory requirements and negligible computational overhead. This self-adjoint computation is reduced to a simple post-process of the field solution which can be applied with any commercial FDTD-based solver. We show that the detection of scatterers such as breast tumors can be achieved with a single system analysis by computing the wideband Jacobian maps of high-fidelity patient-specific tissue models.

articleTitle: Layout design considerations for 60 GHZ SiGe power amplifiers
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this work we report on the importance of electromagnetic analysis for the layout design of monolithic 60 GHz power amplifiers (PA) in SiGe HBT technology. To facilitate this, two different layouts of the same circuit architecture were investigated. The circuits were originally designed using the circuit simulator of Agilentpsilas ADStrade and realized in a high performance 0.25 mum SiGe BiCMOS process with f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub> ap 200 GHz. The two implementations differ only in the layout arrangement of the power stage transistors. Though the simulations without electromagnetic analysis for the power stage showed very similar results for both layout versions, the measurements disagreed seriously. 2frac12 D-EM analyses of both layouts using ADS-Momentumtrade were performed to clarify this issue. The EM post simulations delivered a good agreement with measurements and the frequency shift of the small signal gain could be explained this way. With one layout version a very good overall power performance was achieved: 15 dBm output power with 19.7 % PAE at 61 GHz.

articleTitle: Advanced power amplifiers for modern comunications systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this contribution the research activities and trends in the field of RF and microwave power amplifiers design are discussed. Design strategies for high efficiency and high linearity amplifiers are focused and several state-of-the-art power amplifier design example employing GaN technology are presented. In particular, for each design methodology an actual design realised in hybrid form will be discussed highlighting the different trade-off to be done.

articleTitle: A hybrid AOA — TDOA signal source localization algorithm
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The problem of estimating the position of a radiating source from angle of arrival (bearing) and time difference of arrival measurements taken from passive system in two dimensional case is discussed. The very simple localization algorithm is presented and investigated. Geometric interpretation of algorithm is shown. The problem for stationary both transmitter and receivers is considered.

articleTitle: Antenna effects in detection of 100 GHZ radiation by high electron mobility field-effect transistors
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Detection of 100 GHz electromagnetic radiation by a GaAs/AlGaAs high electron mobility field-effect transistor was investigated at 300 K. The radiation was linearly polarized and measurements were carried out as a function of the angle r between the direction of polarization and the symmetry axis of the transistor. Source-drain photovoltage measured showed the angular dependence A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> cos<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(α − α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) + C with A0; α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and C dependent on the electrical polarization of the transistor gate. A response of the transistor chip (including bonding wires and the substrate) to 100 GHz radiation was numerically simulated. Results of calculations confirmed experimentally observed dependencies and allowed to give the interpretation to the origin of the measured signal as resulting from excitation of two effective oscillators.

articleTitle: Tapered PIFA antenna for handsets terminals
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A new compact PIFA applicable to PCS system is described. The principle aim in design is to broaden the bandwidth within limited body thickness of mobile phones. To overcome the narrow bandwidth characteristics that is typical of a patch antenna a type of tapered patch is employed. The antenna is designed using Zeland Software Ltd and its characteristics are compared with a basic PIFA with similar volume. For WLAN lower 1.8GHz-band, bandwidth of about 14 to 16%, and gain 2.2 dBi were achieved.

articleTitle: Multilayer time domain transmission line model
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The multilayer time domain transmission line model of ground penetrating radar (GPR) has been described in the paper. It is comprehensive and helpful in understanding basic principles of GPR and its main limitations. What is more one can use the model to simulate effectiveness of the radar in specific situations, as long as it can estimate the layer characteristics for the model.

articleTitle: Generalized wire medium and applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the present paper the eigensolutions are presented for the double wire medium where the wire grid geometry is different in orthogonal directions. This is the generalization of the material with symmetric wire grid. The asymmetry in grid geometry results in different plasma numbers in the effective medium model of permittivity. The eigensolutions are ordinary and extraordinary waves. There are three extraordinary waves, one at the low frequency region, one near the plasma frequency and one in between depending on the difference in plasma numbers. Wave propagation and power transportation are studied. The two plasma numbers gives us tuning parameters for obtaining desired propagating properties.

articleTitle: Implementation of matrix-type FDTD algorithm on a graphics accelerator
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents initial conclusions concerning the implementation of matrix-type FDTD algorithm on a low cost graphics accelerator (Nvidia GeForce GT 512 MB, 1.188 GHz) in CUDA (compute unified device architecture). Authors of this article pose a question as to whether using the graphics accelerator based on SIMD architecture (single instruction, multiple data) is reasonable in programming a matrix-type FDTD algorithm, then results of tests meant to compare the efficiency of sequential and parallel implementation are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of quasi-static assumption in nonlinear FinFET model
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The construction and validation of a quasi-static nonlinear microwave model for FinFETs are investigated. A very good agreement between model simulations and measurements is obtained under different DC bias points, input power levels, fundamental frequencies up to 5 GHz, and device geometries. Since the intrinsic part of the FET model is based on the quasi-static approximation, the goal of this work is to analyze in detail the limitations of this assumption by examining the intrinsic admittance parameters versus the frequency.

articleTitle: Design and investigation of a travelling wave amplifier in SOI CMOS with bulk contacts for operation up to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The design of a travelling wave amplifier in silicon on insulator CMOS technology with operation up to 40 GHz is presented. Bulk contacts are implemented to avoid undesired memory effects. The influence of the applied bulk voltage is investigated. At 50 Omega terminations and 2 V times 38 mA supply power, a gain of more than 10 dB and 8 dB are measured up to 26 GHz and 40 GHz, respectively. Between 1 GHz and 10 GHz, the noise figure is below 6 dB.

articleTitle: Programmable 2.4 GHz signal source for testing of the power stages in modern radiocommunication systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes the development and implementation of the Programmable RF (radio frequency) signal source operating with quadrature obtained modulation schemes over a 2divide2.5GHz frequency range and the output power level of -5dBm. The module is based on SDR (software defined radio) architecture with Zero-IF up-conversion and in-baseband modulation signal processing. It characterizes a relatively simple construction and high reconfigurability. Presented measurement results of 2.4GHz PA (power amplifier) and 2.4GHzharr3.5GHz transverter verify acceptable parameters of the devices.

articleTitle: Microwave pulses propagation inside of a 3D heart model
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The electrodynamical rigorous solution of Maxwellpsilas equations related to the microwave pulse propagation inside a three-dimension heart model is presented in this article. The boundary problem was solved by using the singular integral equationspsila method. The carrier microwave frequency is 5 GHz. The modulating signal is rectangular video pulses with the on-off time ratio equal to 2. The model heart was limited by a noncoordinate shape surface and it consisted of two different size cavities. The heart cavities were schematic images of the left and right atriums and ventricles. In our calculations the cavities were filled with blood and the walls of the heart consisted of myocardium tissue. The microwave electric field distributions was analysed at two longitudinal cross-sections of the heart model. It is shown that the microwave electric field distribution inside of the heart model notably depends on the distance and direction from an antenna tip.

articleTitle: Measurement of microwave signals intrapulse parameters by means of IFM methods
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Intrapulse parameters of the microwave signal contain information about source of this signal or about device, which this signal passed through. This information can be obtained with the using so called instantaneous frequency measurement IFM methods. These methods are very fast and utilize microwave phase discriminators MPD and microwave frequency discriminators MFD. The abilities to use MFD for measurement of intrapulse parameters of: simple microwave signal, signal with LFM, signal with PSK, signal with FSK, were described in the paper. There has been presented theoretical descriptions and results of experiments.

articleTitle: A low-cost direct conversion transmitter suitable for multi-OFDM ultra wide band
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper a low-cost direct-conversion UWB transmitter, based on single balanced sub-harmonic mixers, is described. The UWB transmitter prototype is implemented by a laboratory set-up composed of subsystems designed and fabricated in hybrid technology. The key subsystems are represented by the IQ up-converters, each of them consisting of two couple of anti-parallel diodes connected by a wideband balun. The measurements highlight a conversion loss ranging from 12 dB to 15 dB, and a minimum isolation, related to second order LO harmonic, of 53 dB. Due to the diodes characteristic no DC supply is needed and the optimum functionality is achieved with a LO power of 7 dBm. The transmitter includes power splitter for the LO distribution to the IQ mixers, the power combiner and a band-pass output filter. All the subsystems are optimized in the 3.1-4.8 GHz band. Finally, in order to assess the transmitter performances in a realistic environment, system level simulations have been performed compliant with MBOA specifications.

articleTitle: A technique of stabilizing FDTD-subgridding algorithm using reciprocity principle
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper shows the application of reciprocity principle in stabilization procedure for finite difference time domain (FDTD) schemes containing locally refined meshes. The method, originally proposed only for verification of stability of FDTD-subgridding algorithms, allows one to change coupling factors between boundary field samples in such a way, that the resulting scheme will be stable. The presented methodology is verified by numerical tests confirm the stability of a modified subgridding algorithm.

articleTitle: 0.8–4 GHz high efficiency power amplifier in GaN technology
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this contribution, the design and full characterisation of a high efficiency ultra-wide-band power amplifier are presented. The amplifier, based on GaN technology device, has been designed using a CAD oriented broad band matching approach for both input and output networks. The continuous wave measurements results in an average drain efficiency around 50% from 0.8 GHz to 4 GHz with an output power higher than 32 dBm in the overall bandwidth.

articleTitle: Optimization of radio base station placement for localization of moving terminals indoors
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present new method of placing radio stations used for solving geolocation problem in indoor applications. It takes advantages of use neural networks, winner takes most algorithm, resilience phenomenon, Brownian motion and Monte Carlo method. This allow to significantly reduce time needed to compute optimal position of radio stations, while keeping good precision of calculation.

articleTitle: Modular Wireless Sensor Network Platform for RF Transceiver Evaluation
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper shows a modular approach that can be used during the design of wireless sensor nodes. Universal connection between modules, that has been proposed, allows one to design newer versions of nodes in several days instead of weeks. Several modules constructed with this methodology turned out to be reliable platform for evaluation of different RF transceivers.

articleTitle: Visible window image model of ray tracing technique for radio wave propagation
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of an efficient algorithm, which calculates all possible ray paths in the indoor environment. The algorithm is based on the scan all visible virtual images of the transmitter for each visible segment. All reflections from the horizontal plane are assumed, and one order reflection from the ceiling and ground.

articleTitle: About one method of suppression of passive hindrances
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Using difficult signals we get possibility of indemnification of passive hindrances in the single-channel system of radio monitoring due to the use of correlation and spectral characteristics of certain class of difficult signals. One type of such signals are polyphase signals formed on the base of generalized Frankpsilas codes (GFC) with parameters p=0, 5. The algorithm of forming of such signals is offered by authors, and the results of researches of such signals are published in [1].

articleTitle: Class-E tuned amplifiers in power amplitude modulators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A HF power amplifier used in drain amplitude modulator must have a linear static modulation characteristic i.e. linear dependence of amplifier HF output voltage vs. its supply voltage. This condition essential for obtaining low-level envelope distortions is theoretically met by a class-E amplifier. In this paper the influence of non-linear output capacitance of the transistor in the class-E amplifier on its static modulation characteristic is analyzed. Simulations with PSPICE of class-E amplifiers operating at frequencies 0.5 MHz, 5 MHz and 7 MHz have proven that distortions of the amplifier static modulation characteristic caused by non-linear output capacitance of the amplifier transistor are only slight. However, the decrease of power efficiency of the class E amplifier resulting from non-linearity of transistor output capacitance can be significant even by 40%.

articleTitle: Ultra high speed wireless communication in the 250 – 300 GHz band
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Wireless communication is developing very rapidly both in speed and quality. Several new standards are emerging every year and try to find its place in new application domains. The work presented here addresses currently not reachable speeds in the range of 100 Gb/s and more at frequency bands of approximately 250 GHz. It is highly explorative and should indicate current road-blocks and suggest, how to remove some of them. We consider the project as a success if we come close to our original goals and if we succeeded to show that such high speeds are feasible at the indicated frequency band.

articleTitle: X-band substrate integrated waveguide power combiner/divider
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this study an X-band SIRW power divider/combiner structure was designed using a cheap dual layer PCB. The designed structure was then simulated and optimized design was fabricated. The critical analysis of the simulated and the measured results was performed. The final results were very close to the expected results with −3.17dB output and −32dB return loss.

articleTitle: COLUMBUS system integration and verification approach
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper addresses the design and verification of the Columbus avionics architecture which has been successfully commissioned in-orbit after the docking of the Columbus module to the International Space Station on the 10 th of February 2008. The avionics of the Columbus module has been designed around a layered architecture and is based on state-of-the-art early 1990's space technologies. The avionics provides the necessary controllability and observability of the vital and nominal functions of the module, including the interface with the space station. It also provides all the necessary resources for crew support and for the internal and external payloads utilisation. An important step towards the successful commissioning was the in verification approach followed during the assembly, Integration and Testing phase of the Project. The integration and validation philosophy used consists of an overall electrical test model (ETM), representing all the module functionalities, based on classic electrical model (EM) at box level mixed with simulators replacing the missing functionalities such as redundancies and environmental subsystems (thermal and environmental life control system). The ETM approach, based on EM box and simulators, had also the advantage to reduce the cost and to increase at the same time the verification flexibility. Moreover it allowed upgradeability without compromising verification quality. Special care had been given to the verification of the payloads racks through the ETM upgrade to support interface validation with the Columbus module even after it had been delivered to the ISS. Furthermore, all means for additional communication systems have been foreseen to increase the downlink and uplink capabilities of the Columbus Laboratory when external RF or optical terminals will be implemented. Finally, the Columbus avionics has been designed to allow future expansions such as the amateur radio for ISS (ARISS) project for which external antennas have been pre-installed.

articleTitle: Statistical modelling of wideband propagation channel in an indoor environment
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper concerns a statistical modelling of wideband radio propagation channel in an indoor environment. An approach of describing amplitudes and excess delays of particular multipath components by means of probability density functions (PDF) was developed. Analysed channel impulse response (CIR) realizations were obtained from frequency-domain measurements carried out in a large laboratory hall.

articleTitle: Circular array of triangular patches as filter
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper proposed a microstrip circular array antenna consist of 8 triangular patches work as a filter for weak signals (noise) and undesired signals in L-band of microwave frequency. This array has been designed on YIG substrate which works on the principle of inverse dynamic nonlinearity of magnetostatic waves in ferrite substrates. The proposed antenna structure is suitable for mobile communication system.

articleTitle: Deriving characteristics of the slotline using the conformal mapping technique
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, the conformal mapping technique is applied to obtained closed-form expressions for calculating the characteristic impedance and the effective dielectric constant of the slotline. The presented expressions take into account the finite width of the strips of the slotline, the case often omitted in other works. The validity of the presented expressions is tested in a number of examples. The obtained results are compared with those obtained from the full-wave electromagnetic analyses. Good agreement is noted in all of the considered cases.

articleTitle: Electric field distributions in the cross-sections of the metamaterial hollow-core and rod waveguides
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Here we present an investigation of the electric field distributions in the cross-sections of the cylindrical metamaterial hollow-core and rod waveguides. The radius of the cylindrical waveguides is r = 3 mm and the azimuthal index m = 1. We have calculated the electric field distributions for the main and three higher modes, propagating in the metamaterial hollow-core waveguide. We have also calculated the electric field distribution of the main mode propagating in the metamaterial rod waveguide. Our calculations were made at the frequencies f = 100 and 112.5 GHz. The calculation results show that the electric field distributions in the waveguide cross section for the different frequencies and modes as well as for different waveguide geometries are strong dissimilar to each other. The electric field distribution of the waveguide main mode is unlike for double and single negative metamaterial. We are aware of the fact that the electric field penetrates into metamaterial of all investigated waveguides.

articleTitle: Methods of improving accuracy of indoor localization systems based on 802.11 standard infrastructure
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper focuses on various methods of increasing accuracy of existing localization algorithms implemented in WLAN 802.11 infrastructure. In this paper we present a novel approach based on combination of various enhancement methods such as algorithms interworks, environment adapting and signal filtering. Increased accuracy is shown with results of tests performed on exemplary system.

articleTitle: “Integrated front-end modules at millimeter waves frequencies - Focus on integrated antennas and associated functions for mobile and wireless applications”
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Recently, with a rapid spread of Internet, wireless LANs have been widely deployed in companies, public areas and home environments. Because of the ease of installation and low maintenance cost, wireless LANs are becoming popular solutions for many applications. In this context, companies investigate today on the next generation of wireless LANs for providing higher capabilities to customers. Data transfer from high resolution digital cameras, transfer of video and multimedia contents between computers and portable devices are considered as potential emerging mass-production applications; Wireless 1 Gbits/s LAN will certainly concurrence gigabit Ethernet links in a near future in our domestic environment, and we are investigating on such technologies.

articleTitle: Silicon CPW coupled-lines meta-material coupler and on-wafer characterization using a 2-port vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A coupled-line coupler based on two coupled artificial composite right/left-handed transmission lines (CRLH TLs) fabricated on high resistivity silicon substrate using coplanar waveguides (CPW) is designed, fabricated and on-wafer experimentally characterized. The CRLH TL consists of series CPW interdigital capacitors and parallel short-ended CPWs. For this four-port circuit, the on-wafer experimental results have been obtained using a two-port vector analyzer following a method which is also presented.

articleTitle: Development of a power-efficient, high-gain, low-noise ultra-wideband 0.18-μm CMOS distributed amplifier
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A distributed amplifier with new cascade inductively-coupled common-source gain-cell configuration is presented. Compared with other existing gain-cell configurations, the proposed cascade common-source gain cell provides much higher gain. The new distributed amplifier, fabricated in TSMC 0.18-mum CMOS process, achieves an average power gain of around 10 dB, input match of less than -20 dB, and noise figure of 3.3-6.1dB with an unprecedented power consumption of only 19.6 mW over the entire ultra-wideband (UWB) band of 3.1-10.6 GHz. In the high-gain operating mode that consumes 100 mW, the new CMOS distributed amplifier provides an unprecedented power gain of 16 dB with 3.2-6-dB noise figure over the UWB range.

articleTitle: Evaluation of RMSC application in saw RFIDS
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A novel design of SAW-tags in which the reversing multistrip couplers are exploited for the SAW reflection is proposed and evaluated by numerical analysis. Results are promising indicating perspective applications in the phase-coded tags, and pulse coded tags, as well.

articleTitle: Lumped element network synthesis for one-port passive microwave structures
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: A network oriented approach to passive microwave circuits modeling provides compact representation of the circuit and leads to the reduction of the required computer time and memory capacity. The proposed stability criterion allows splitting the simulation results into two parts representing a lumped elements model and distributed parameters model. The system identification procedure has been applied for the extraction of the lumped element model parameters of the scattering transfer function. The lumped elements network realization for the input impedance of the wide band bowtie antenna is presented.

articleTitle: Weakly singular surface integral equations for microstrip discontinuities and nonregular structure applications
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: An original technique reducing the kernel singularities of surface impedance and admittance equations have been developed and new types of surface integral equations with integrable kernels have been introduced. The new equations are based on the representation of surface vector functions through two scalar potentials using the Green's formulas, or on the inverse operator-function implementation. The numerical results for microstrip resonators, for dispersion characteristics of microstrip lines and for microstrip open end are presented.

articleTitle: The bulk and surface helicons in the regularly inhomogeneous semiconductor structure
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper the surface waves propagated along the contact of two periodic semiconductor lattices placed in the external magnetic field is considered. Magnetic field vector is situated in the same plane where electromagnetic waves propagate. Parameterspsila region is investigated where the helicon waves propagate. The distinctive feature of the helicon wave spectrum is that the numerous narrow allowed zones arise. It is shown that near the edge of the bulk helicon transmission band the surface helicon wave exist.

articleTitle: Influence of antennas characteristics on accuracy of TOA indoor positioniong systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents analysis of dependence of distance determination error in localization system based on time of arrival (TOA) measurements, on beam width of antenna radiation pattern. Using narrow beam antennas some multipath components with small delays, causing errors of calculation of distance between antennas, can be eliminated and accuracy of the system can be increased. Analysis bases on results of raytracing simulations, used to determine parameters of the propagation channel for considered configuration of indoor environment. Dependence on system bandwidth and detection method implemented in the system have also considered during the analysis. This research is part of EU VI FP RESOLUTION project which goal is to develop accurate positioning system operating in an indoor rich scattering environment, i.e. factory halls.

articleTitle: Simultaneous microwave electric field and temperature measurement using pigtailed electro-optic probes
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: We present here the design of a novel electro-optic probe and its associated optical bench, providing microwave electric field measurements together with the temperature. The sensor with its fully automated optical bench presents very good spatial and temporal resolutions, almost no invasiveness, a frequency bandwidth from a few kHz up to tens of GHz with a sensitivity of 0.7 V.m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1/2</sup> and a temperature accuracy of 40 mK. This latter characteristic is obtained thanks to a servo-controlled system that has been developed to stabilise the electro-optic response of the sensors and hence to allow reliable electric field measurements under outdoors conditions over long time durations exceeding several tens of minutes.

articleTitle: Scattering performance of a composed ferrite-dielectric rotary- field phase shifter section
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The simulated scattering characteristics are presented for a section of circular waveguide filled with a rod consisting of a number of alternating ferrite and dielectric discs which are magnetized through a four pole magnetic field. The advantage of this waveguide structure is reduction of size to a fraction of the diameters needed for ferrite filled waveguide section. The simulated performance indicates application of this configuration as phase shifters and polarizers.

articleTitle: Automated detection of moving person from small pulse battlefield radar
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents algorithm for automatic detection of moving person, utilizing signal from small pulse battlefield radar. The automation process presumes real signal analysis from radar coherent channel, signatures recognition for aimed specific group of targets, following signal preprocessing to enhance the most suitable expected signal parameters and reduce jamming compounds and final appropriate algorithm development with respect to specific application constrains. The analytic portion was realized on the real moving persons (equipped with corner reflector) measurement basis and further algorithm verification on real samples of moving persons.

articleTitle: Grouping macromodels by using multilevel model order reduction
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This article introduces a novel technique of grouping macromodels for the FDTD method. The new technique is based on the multilevel model order reduction scheme. Macromodel grouping allows one to increase the simulation speed in comparison to not-grouped macromodels with the same good (or even better) accuracy. The scheme uses the ENOR algorithm for efficient model order reduction.

articleTitle: Nonlinear switching of microwave pulses in layered media with paraelectric
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Interaction of microwave electromagnetic (EM) waves with a layered structure that includes a paraelectric is investigated theoretically. An oblique incidence of EM wave is considered, when the total internal reflection and resonant transmission at several frequencies occur. In is demonstrated that this structure modulates effectively EM wave. The modulation mechanism is a change of dielectric permittivity of a paraelectric layer in a moderate bias electric field. An interaction of strong incident EM pulses with this structure is also considered in the case of absence of a bias electric field. The nonlinear switching of short pulses takes place there, when both the maximum amplitude and the shape of a pulse change essentially under a small change of the amplitude of the incident pulse.

articleTitle: Reduction of dispersion induced distortions by semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: An approach is presented to reduce the chromatic dispersion-induced distortions in optical links carrying combined baseband and microwave signals. This new method is based on the interplay of intensity dependent phase modulation in semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) and fiber nonlinearities. Theoretical and experimental results are demonstrated for a 400 km long optical link.

articleTitle: Method for improving resonance isolators
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: E-plane resonance isolator behaviour is reviewed in this article, focusing on the change in the reflection coefficient, when the shape of the ferrite is modified. The examinations of the different structures were carried out by the Microwave Studio 3-dimensional EM field simulation software.

articleTitle: Free-space optical communications using quantum cascade laser
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper presents construction of broadband optical system devoted to free space optical communication using long wavelength quantum cascade laser and a heterostructural thermally cooled HgCdTe photodetector. This system should characterize with lower sensitivity to adverse meteorological conditions when compared with the systems operating in near IR.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the effects of polarization on the measured radiation efficiency of a dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The radiation efficiencies of two rectangular dielectric resonant antennas (DRAs) were investigated using the directivity/ gain (D/G) method and the Wheeler cap method. Both antennas are linearly polarized but have different linear polarization purities. Through comparison of their radiation efficiencies, itpsilas shown that the polarization purity strongly affects the D/G measurement of the DRAspsila radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Wave diffraction for nondestructive analysis
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Some aspects of engineering materials non-destructive testing (NDT) are represented in terms of its application to the fracture mechanics. The active NDT methods which utilize of the sounding or stimulated physical fields as well as the acoustic emission analysis of materialpsilas space damaging and the inspection information processing are considered briefly. The modern concept of the NDT methods development for the purposes of technical diagnostics is formulated.

articleTitle: A portable dielectric-property determination system using coupled antennas
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper presents a dielectric-property determination system that measures magnitude of reflection and coupling coefficients of coupled antennas. They are plotted on a ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>′ ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>″ plane, and the intersection of these two quantities provides the value of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>′ and ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>″. Measurement results of paddy validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique. The system provides accurate results. The error from the results of proposed system differs from the use of network analyzer of less than 4 %.

articleTitle: Broadband Matching for Ferroelectric Film Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Due to big permittivity, ferroelectric film microwave phase shifter has reduced impedance and therefore needs matching as with the oscillator so with the antenna devices. Elaborated matching section uses the same film that phase shifter and provides as matching so its automatic adaptation to the change in film permittivity during phase shifter operation.

articleTitle: Parameters determination of symmetrical microwave two-ports
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Matching conditions for passive symmetrical microwave two-ports with an arbitrary connect structure and component types have been determined. A classification of such two-ports with regard of the matching conditions has been validated. For parametric mismatched two-ports a relation between input admittances of the proper one-ports has been determined. The admittance values have been found for given transmission and reflection coefficients. A method for definition of parameters of mismatched two-ports with a predetermined structure, belonging to the subset of parametric mismatched two-ports has been proposed. The application of the proposed method is illustrated by examples of parameter calculations for circuits with different component bases as well experiments conducted with the circuits.

articleTitle: Multi-band vco based on distributed VCO and switched-capacitors banks
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The paper introduces a new approach for the design of multi-band distributed VCOs for mobile TLC applications. The techniques exploits the potentialities of a switched-capacitor approach, joint to, the versatility of a distribute VCO. The design procedure is discussed. The measured characteristics of a hybrid prototype are reported, validating the potentialities of the approach.

articleTitle: Critical analysis for design of HF radio link in Brazil
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) transmission between 3 and 30 MHz by ITU convention is called high frequency (HF) or shortwave radio. HF is widely used communication band for long distances. The use of HF radio transmission has been experiencing a renewal of interest and investment in Europe and USA, because of the realization that satellite and terrestrial communication modes are vulnerable to electronic countermeasures and physical destruction HF radio transmission, although of much lower overall reliability and limited data bandwidth than other communication bands, allow communication over long distances the level of recovery furnished by HF is much more improved than the case of satellite and terrestrial communication modes. In Brazil meanwhile this frequency mode is quite unusual and the official documentation provided by the Brazilian official agency called ANATEL for the radio link conception is not complete and it has many mistakes. This paper propose to make an overall about the topics that are important in the radio-link conception and also propose some differential steps in the HF prediction, some useful aspects of system design not afforded in the rules of the Brazilian agency and a critical analysis of the possible used HF antennas.

articleTitle: Emerging technologies for modern communications and radar systems
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper discussed a variety of enabling technologies that complement the realization of highly integrated, multifunctional transceiver based systems. Key examples of reconfigurable components will be presented. Adaptive analog front end technology will be discussed to complement digital signal processing to realize mixed signal solutions that provide for fast, flexible and low power consumption with minimal resources. Examples of adaptable analog technologies include adaptable filtering and multi-resolution spectral processing and adaptable, reconfigurable antennas and matching networks. One example is a a highly integrated all CMOS UHF receiver with spectral sensing in 180 nm CMOS with ~1M gates and 100mW total power consumption. In the future, an order of magnitude increase in integration and an order of magnitude reduction in power consumption is expected. Complementary technology for a digital phased array will also be discussed. Required hardware and signal processing capabilities are being developed as part of an integrated digital array radar antenna/prototype. Very high power solid state wideband gap technology is being used together with low cost surface mount technology to realize a low cost, air cooled, light weight antenna array.
