articleTitle: Optimalization and improvement of operation in microwave oscillators by using optical analog link
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper we present an idea of improvement of operation in microwave oscillators by using microwave - light interactions. A comparison between classic solution and analog optical link solution is presented, as well as obtained simulation results.

articleTitle: Biological interaction of pulse-modulated electromagnetic fields and protection of humans from exposure to fields emitted from radars
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: In the paper characteristics of pulse-modulated radiation emitted from radars have been presented and a brief overview of interaction of such microwave fields with biological body has been revealed. Thermal and non-thermal effects of pulsed fields evoked in the organisms were discussed and thresholds for these effects in humans and animals were pointed out. Polish standards and Directive recommendations and guidelines providing protection of people against adverse health effects have also been presented.

articleTitle: Phase center measurements of the double ridged antenna with a three-channel method
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: The phase center measurement results of double-ridged antenna at 0.76–2.5 GHz has been presented. The three-channel method was used for phase center location. This method is based on the measurements of power of microwave signals received by two antennas separately and on measurement of power of vector sum of these signals.

articleTitle: Recent development of mimo antennas and their evaluation for small mobile terminals
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: This paper discusses the antenna configurations in small mobile terminals for MIMO (multiple-in-multiple-out) systems. It is very challenging to fit several antennas with low correlation, high efficiency and adequate bandwidth, as required in MIMO communications systems, into such devices, whose length is typically about 100 mm. Moreover, in the future MIMO techniques may be utilised at several frequency ranges starting probably from as low as 500 MHz like in UHF handheld TV receivers and ranging to over 5 GHz like in multiband OFDM based UWB systems. The paper presents some visions how all these antenna configurations might be realized in the very limited space available in the mobile terminal. As in such cases the performance of the antennas is far from ideal, it is also very important to be able to estimate the behaviour of the antenna configurations in realistic usage conditions already at the design phase of the antennas and systems. In this paper we describe the Measurement Based Antenna Test-bed (MEBAT) for the evaluation of mobile terminal antennas for MIMO systems. The method combines data from a measured directional channel library and the radiation patterns of antennas under test. The patterns can be either simulated or measured e.g. with the Rapid Antenna Measurement System (RAMS). The RAMS system enables to define the radiation properties of mobile terminal antenna systems in very short time also in the case, when a real test person is used in the measurement. Examples of performance evaluations with the MEBAT system are given for realistic MIMO antenna configurations for mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Solving design and inverse-imaging problems through electromagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: MIKON 2008 - 17th International Conference on Microwaves, Radar and Wireless Communications
abstract: Numerical electromagnetic analysis has been rapidly developing for more than three decades now, matching closely the remarkable progress of computing technology. Commercial packages for high-frequency computer-aided analysis are nowadays standard toolboxes in industrial and academic microwave laboratories. Yet designers and researchers rarely use full-wave simulations in the early to intermediate stages of the design process. The usual practice is to use them only as a final verification tool before prototyping. This is not for the lack of suitable optimization algorithms as these have grown to no lesser degree of sophistication and commercialization than electromagnetic solvers. The weakest link in electromagnetic computer-aided design is that between the simulation and the optimization algorithms. In this talk, we review the latest developments in simulation-based optimization in microwave engineering. We outline the requirements of optimization algorithms in design and inverse problems, and we discuss how electromagnetic simulators must improve to meet these demands. We illustrate the importance of these developments through design and microwave-imaging examples.
